items.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: when I’m out on the road with Freddie Hubbard, and I always bug him because I want to know everything

ctx.x: You know one professor that I studied with, he basically he said, you know he said let’s say you’re getting ready to play over this dominant seven with a flat nine or a sharp nine. And you’re getting ready to play symmetric diminished half step whole step. He said, don’t play the whole scale two octaves. In other words he said we know you know the scale, he said, hint at it and then give the audience some place to enter the music. Let the thing breathe long enough for them to enter. Because if they’re listening,…

Well a lot of times too, if like when I’m out on the road with Freddie Hubbard, and I always bug him because I want to know everything. And Freddie told me this himself, if you notice the thing about Freddie, he has the command to go either way. But he prefers to phrase. Because phrasing is like talking to somebody. You know if you’re going to play on that dominant seven flat five, why play a scale? You know the scale that it goes with, so why play [scats]. That really doesn’t mean anything except that you know…

I’ve got a definition I want to ask you about. Because this is kind of elusive, but you just give us your own words. You know playing rhythm guitar, setting up sometimes counter rhythms. If the bass is walking quarter notes, and sometimes you have to drop chords and spaces all around without, without, sometimes without doing the Freddie Green thing on every beat. But can you give us your definition of what you would call groove. What is groove?
